title: Self Dividing Numbers
summary: Identify all self-dividing numbers within the range [left, right], where a self-dividing number is defined as a number that is divisible by each of its digits, and none of its digits are zero.
statement: Identify all self-dividing numbers within the range [left, right], where a self-dividing number is defined as a number that is divisible by each of its digits, and none of its digits are zero.
constraints: A self-dividing number contains no zero and is divisible by each of its digits.
hints: Every decimal digit supplies an independent divisibility requirement, and zero always rejects the number.
Inspect digits with repeated division by ten.
While digit is nonzero and divides original, discard it; accept only after all digits are consumed.
The loop invariant says all removed digits were nonzero divisors of the original value.
editorial: The loop invariant says all removed digits were nonzero divisors of the original value.

tests.explanation: The qualifying values are 1 through 9, then 11, 12, 15, and 22.
Only 48 is divisible by both four and eight.
